TERM-STROOP-INTERFERENCE.label: Stroop interference effect
TERM-STROOP-INTERFERENCE.definition: The delay in naming the ink colour of a colour word when the word names a different colour, relative to a neutral baseline.
indicators: longer colour-naming times in the incongruent condition than in the neutral condition
effect measured at the level of a participant sample
TERM-STROOP-INTERFERENCE.distinguishing_test: Compare against the NEUTRAL baseline, not only against the congruent condition: a delay versus neutral is interference; part of the congruent-incongruent gap can be facilitation.

sources.ref: Stroop, J. R. (1935), 'Studies of interference in serial verbal reactions', Journal of Experimental Psychology, 18(6), 643-662
sources.access_note: bibliographic record confirmed via the Crossref API on 2026-11-12 (title, journal, volume, issue, pages, DOI); full text NOT read; findings not reproduced here

sources.ref: MacLeod, C. M. (1991), 'Half a century of research on the Stroop effect: An integrative review', Psychological Bulletin, 109(2), 163-203
sources.access_note: bibliographic record confirmed via the Crossref API on 2026-11-12; full text NOT read; it is cited as the standard review, not as a source whose argument was checked here

TERM-STROOP-INTERFERENCE.claim_limit: A population-level experimental effect. It cannot certify interference in a single participant or a single trial.

TERM-STROOP-FACILITATION.label: Stroop facilitation effect
TERM-STROOP-FACILITATION.definition: The speed-up in naming the ink colour when the word names the same colour, relative to a neutral baseline.
indicators: shorter colour-naming times in the congruent condition than in the neutral condition
TERM-STROOP-FACILITATION.distinguishing_test: Is the measured difference below (faster) or above (slower) the neutral baseline? Without a neutral condition, interference and facilitation cannot be separated.

sources.ref: MacLeod, C. M. (1991), 'Half a century of research on the Stroop effect: An integrative review', Psychological Bulletin, 109(2), 163-203
sources.access_note: bibliographic record confirmed via the Crossref API on 2026-11-12; full text NOT read; the interference/facilitation distinction is standard terminology, not a quotation read here

TERM-STROOP-FACILITATION.claim_limit: A population-level experimental effect; not observable in one trial.

TERM-CONGRUENT-TRIAL.label: congruent trial
TERM-CONGRUENT-TRIAL.definition: A trial where the word meaning and the ink colour match.
indicators: stimulus_word and stimulus_ink carry the same colour name
TERM-CONGRUENT-TRIAL.distinguishing_test: Do word and ink match? Matching is congruent; mismatching is incongruent; a non-colour word is the neutral condition, not a congruent one.

sources.ref: Stroop, J. R. (1935), 'Studies of interference in serial verbal reactions', Journal of Experimental Psychology, 18(6), 643-662
sources.access_note: bibliographic record confirmed via the Crossref API on 2026-11-12; full text NOT read

TERM-CONGRUENT-TRIAL.claim_limit: A stimulus condition label. It says nothing about a participant's response.

TERM-INCONGRUENT-TRIAL.label: incongruent trial
TERM-INCONGRUENT-TRIAL.definition: A trial where the word meaning and the ink colour conflict.
indicators: stimulus_word names a different colour than stimulus_ink
TERM-INCONGRUENT-TRIAL.distinguishing_test: Do word and ink conflict? Conflict is incongruent; match is congruent; non-colour words belong to the neutral condition.

sources.ref: Stroop, J. R. (1935), 'Studies of interference in serial verbal reactions', Journal of Experimental Psychology, 18(6), 643-662

TERM-INCONGRUENT-TRIAL.claim_limit: A stimulus condition label; not a diagnosis and not a trait measure.

TERM-REACTION-TIME.label: reaction time (RT)
TERM-REACTION-TIME.definition: Elapsed time between stimulus onset and the recorded response, measured in milliseconds.
TERM-REACTION-TIME.distinguishing_test: Is the dependent variable response speed or response correctness? A slower mean with unchanged accuracy is a speed effect, not an accuracy effect.

sources.ref: MacLeod, C. M. (1991), 'Half a century of research on the Stroop effect: An integrative review', Psychological Bulletin, 109(2), 163-203
sources.access_note: bibliographic record confirmed via the Crossref API on 2026-11-12; full text NOT read; RT as the standard dependent measure is textbook knowledge, not a quotation read here

TERM-REACTION-TIME.claim_limit: A performance measure. An RT difference alone cannot establish which process caused it.

TERM-RESPONSE-ACCURACY.label: response accuracy
TERM-RESPONSE-ACCURACY.definition: The proportion of correct responses in a condition.
indicators: reported as error rate or per cent correct
TERM-RESPONSE-ACCURACY.distinguishing_test: Is the dependent variable correctness or speed? Under a speed-accuracy tradeoff the two can move in opposite directions and must be reported separately.

TERM-NEUTRAL-CONDITION.label: neutral (baseline) condition
TERM-NEUTRAL-CONDITION.definition: A condition with a non-colour word in a coloured ink, providing the baseline against which interference and facilitation are each measured.
indicators: ink colour drawn from the same colour set
TERM-NEUTRAL-CONDITION.distinguishing_test: Is the word a colour name? If not, the trial is neutral; without this baseline the congruent-incongruent gap conflates interference and facilitation.

TERM-NEUTRAL-CONDITION.claim_limit: A stimulus condition label. Choosing it does not fix how many trials or participants are needed.

THEORY-AUTOMATICITY-ACCOUNT.label: automaticity account of Stroop interference
THEORY-AUTOMATICITY-ACCOUNT.statement: Word reading is highly practised and proceeds automatically, so it competes with the deliberately controlled colour-naming response when word and ink conflict.
explains: why incongruent colour naming is slower than neutral
why the effect is robust across many task variants
does_not_explain: whether a specific participant read the word automatically in a specific trial
the size of the effect in a population the study did not sample
whether automaticity or a capacity limit is the operative cause in a given dataset

sources.ref: MacLeod, C. M. (1991), 'Half a century of research on the Stroop effect: An integrative review', Psychological Bulletin, 109(2), 163-203
sources.access_note: bibliographic record confirmed via the Crossref API on 2026-11-12; full text NOT read; the account as stated here is standard textbook-level theory, NOT a checked quotation from the review

THEORY-AUTOMATICITY-ACCOUNT.claim_limit: A theoretical account of a population-level effect. It cannot certify a mechanism in one dataset; rival accounts remain open (T6 respected here: source verified, claim kept CANDIDATE where appropriate).

THEORY-CAPACITY-ACCOUNT.label: limited-capacity / attentional account
THEORY-CAPACITY-ACCOUNT.statement: Word and colour processing draw on limited-capacity resources; under conflict the shared demand produces the delay, without requiring reading to be automatic.
explains: why interference can appear even when reading is made difficult
why dual-task load can modulate the effect
does_not_explain: why the effect is larger for colour words than for arbitrary distractor words
which resource is exhausted in a specific dataset

sources.ref: MacLeod, C. M. (1991), 'Half a century of research on the Stroop effect: An integrative review', Psychological Bulletin, 109(2), 163-203
sources.access_note: bibliographic record confirmed via the Crossref API on 2026-11-12; full text NOT read; cited as the standard review covering multiple accounts, not as a checked argument

THEORY-CAPACITY-ACCOUNT.claim_limit: A rival account. Its availability means an interference effect alone does not decide between automaticity and capacity.

THEORY-SPEED-ACCURACY-TRADEOFF.label: speed-accuracy tradeoff
THEORY-SPEED-ACCURACY-TRADEOFF.statement: A responder can trade speed for accuracy by shifting response caution; a longer mean response time can therefore reflect a caution shift rather than processing conflict.
explains: why longer times can co-unchanged accuracy
why an RT-only design cannot always separate conflict from caution
does_not_explain: the size of any specific interference effect
why a particular participant shifted caution
